newsitem.title: USA: FTC OKs Baxter buy of Immuno Intl.
newsitem.headline: FTC OKs Baxter buy of Immuno Intl.

text.p: The United States government conditionally cleared the way Thursday for Baxter International Inc. to buy Immuno International AG for about $700 million, creating the world's largest blood products manufacturer.
The Federal Trade Commission announced that Baxter had agreed to sell off its Autoplex product to prevent a monopoly in products needed by many hemophiliacs.
Baxter also agreed to license Immuno's "fibrin sealant," a product used to stop bleeding during surgery, after a traumatic injury and to promote the healing of wounds.
"The Commission has accepted, subject to final approval, an agreement which remedies the anticompetitive effects of the proposed merger," the FTC said in a statement.

Baxter, headquartered in Deerfield, Ill., and Immuno, headquartered in Zollikon, Switzerland, manufacture the only two products available in the United States for hemophiliacs who develop an immune response to the primary treatment for their condition, the FTC said.
Under the agreement, Baxter will sell off its product within four months to a buyer approved by the FTC.
The two companies are two of only a few that manufacture fibrin sealants, for a market the FTC estimates to be as much as $400 million annually in the United States.
The FTC said it was concerned Baxter's acquisition of Immuno would eliminate competition in research and development of fibrin sealants, as well as in their manufacture and sale.
In addition to the price paid by Baxter now, it has up to three years to pay an additional amount that will make the total price about $900 million.
